messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging sasha (on-call): Northstar Financial (tenant ns-42, VPC) is hitting sustained 429s from their dedicated pool. Error rate > 30% over 2m, burst at 4x baseline. Incident ID: INC-2026-31765. Please ack and advise.

sasha (on-call): acked. looking. can someone paste the customer rate/contract? leo?

leo (acct-eng): on it. Northstar is on enterprise VPC with a dedicated pool (ded-pool-07). Contract has committed units up to 500 reqs/s, with negotiated burst allowance to 1500 reqs/s for 10m windows only. they do have a custom SLA that allowed emergency bursts subject to ops approval.

matt (sre): i'm seeing consistent 429s at the ingress gateway for ns-42. Backend serving nodes show full queue saturation and queue drops. KV cache hit is low for this workload. stack traces point to queue throttles, not auth failures.

ada (support): customer reported slow responses and ~15% of requests returned 429s starting ~10:04 UTC. they're in production chatbots. high business impact.

ops-bot: route-check: ded-pool-07 health: 3/6 nodes healthy, cpu/gpu saturation 95%/88%, pending queue length high. Auto-scale policy is "opt-in" for this customer and currently capped by dedicated pool max_size: 6.

oliver (eng-runtime): ok, ded-pool-07 has two nodes OOMed overnight and haven't been replaced due to infra quota. we can either spin extra nodes (if infra quota approved) or do a targeted temporary rate-lift on the control plane to let more tokens through to a fallback variant in hosted region.

sasha (on-call): immediate priority: limit customer impact. options: 1) emergency contract override -> raise burst to 3000 reqs/s for 30m (manual approval required), 2) route ns-42 to fallback hosted fleet (model variant compatible) with degraded throughput but lower latency risk, or 3) isolate noisy sub-tenants and shard traffic. any quick preference?

leo (acct-eng): customer requests full unblock now. they're asking for emergency override for 1 hour while we remediate. i'm ready to sign off pending ops approval. nate (sales) is on the line with their CTO.

nate (sales): confirmed, CTO is available to accept a temporary SLA amendment. they emphasize minimize downtime, they accept model parity loss if needed.

matt (sre): proposing hybrid: give a short contract override (30m) to reduce errors while we spin additional nodes and move noisy prefixes to a fallback variant. we need an admin API call to add a per-tenant override and a routing rule to prefer hosted fallback.

oliver (eng-runtime): I can push the routing change. admin API snippet to create override:```bash
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/api/v1/tenant-overrides \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "tenant_id": "ns-42",
    "override_type": "burst_quota",
    "value": 3000,
    "duration_min": 30,
    "note": "Emergency unblock for production incident INC-2026-31765"
  }'
```

oliver (eng-runtime): and routing rule to prioritize hosted fallback for that tenant:```yaml
- match: tenant == "ns-42"
  action:
    primary: hosted-fallback-model-v2
    fallback: ded-pool-07
    sticky: true
```

sasha (on-call): matt, can you run the override and monitor? i'll coordinate infra to spin nodes. ada, loop the customer ops and update them. leo/nate, please confirm signoff in thread.

matt (sre): running override now. posting audit command output:```json
{"cmd":"create_override","tenant":"ns-42","value":3000,"duration_min":30,"result":"queued","id":"ovr-31765-1"}
```

matt (sre): override accepted by control plane. metrics in ~30s should reflect lower 429s. setting up a short alert to notify when error rate < 5% or after 30m expire.

ops-bot: action-log: override ovr-31765-1 created by matt. routing change queued by oliver. infra-request: node spin-up for ded-pool-07 requested by sasha (ticket INFRA-8421).

oliver (eng-runtime): pushed routing rule. verifying traffic shift... seeing ~40% of ns-42 traffic now routed to hosted-fallback-model-v2, latency slightly higher but successful rate up.

sasha (on-call): infra confirmed nodes 2/2 provisioned for ded-pool-07 (INFRA-8421). bring-up in progress, will re-balance once nodes healthy.

matt (sre): 6m post-override: 429 rate down from 32% -> 3.2%. queue length decreasing. keeping monitor for 30m window.

ada (support): updated customer: "we've applied a temporary unblock and routing fallback; we're provisioning additional capacity and will follow up with timeline. Monitoring shows errors reduced." Customer responded :thumbsup:.

leo (acct-eng): formally document the temporary amendment: agreed to 30m/3000 reqs/s; customer acknowledged. will capture in CRM and finance for billing uplift.

sasha (on-call): post-incident tasks: 1) ensure override ovr-31765-1 expires as scheduled and auto-rollbacks are verified, 2) postmortem + runbook gap update for ded-pool auto-replace, 3) follow-up call with customer in 2h, 4) check cache strategy to improve KV hit for their workload. assigning owners: matt (monitor + expire check), oliver (routing + runbook), leo (customer comms + billing).

matt (sre): noted. i'll create INC ticket and link logs/traces (INC-2026-31765).

nate (sales): thanks team. customer on call is relieved. please ping me if we need sales/legal signoff on longer override.

sasha (on-call): closing loop here — error rates stable, infra healing. leaving temporary override to expire; if anything spikes i'll reopen. tagging for follow-up: #postmortems. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-31765 updated: status -> mitigated, assigned -> matt, oliver, leo, follow-up meeting scheduled.

matt (sre): final note: long-term fix options: enable proactive node replacement, widen auto-scale policy for enterprise pools with signed overrides, and add per-tenant adaptive prefix caching. will include in postmortem."
